accuracy.evidence: Aligns with CCSS K.CC.3 write 0–20 and NC Y1 read/write 1–20 in numerals; teen = 10+ones and digit-order (12 vs 21) match place-value teaching.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets digit swaps (12/21, 16/61), writing 15 as 51, reading 20 as two ones, and mismatching counts to nearby numerals — named in adult text and challenge why().

lab_distinct.evidence: Lab centres on numeral read/write to 20: match, ten-and-ones build, digit pad, 0–20 line, twelve-vs-21 — not a reuse of teens-structure or bonds labs.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learner builds 14 from a ten-rod and ones and writes 16 before the text confirms tens-left ones-right.

predictions.evidence: Predictions offer 17/70, 4 tens and 1 one, 6-first, and sixty-one as tempting wrong readings the tasks then disprove.

challenge_feedback.evidence: why() covers swap, tens, allten, dup, ones, drop, ten, twenty, same, both for specific digit-place slips.

readability.evidence: Short kid sentences for ages 5–6; adult names CCSS/NC and mistakes without filler.

no_filler.evidence: Every sentence defines numeral, teen structure, digit order, or a mistake — no journey/explore padding.

mobile.evidence: Digit pad and large lbtn targets; bead drag on number line; young shell layout.

accessibility.evidence: Buttons mirror drag actions; say() updates aria-label; challenge aria-live status.
